skill.name: subagent-driven-development
skill.description: Guides agents through plan execution by assigning one independent task at a time to fresh subagents, then requiring review before moving to the next task.
skill.summary: Execute development plans with fresh task subagents and review checkpoints.
skill.author: DYAI2025

content.value_statement: Complex implementation plans can lose quality when one agent keeps too much context. This skill assigns each task to a fresh subagent and adds review checkpoints before progress continues.
actual_capabilities: Defines when to use subagent-driven execution for mostly independent plan tasks.
Provides a repeatable task loop for dispatching fresh implementation subagents.
Requires code review after each completed task before moving forward.
Describes how to handle critical, important, and minor review findings.
Connects the workflow to planning, code review, TDD, and branch completion skills.
limitations: It assumes the plan already exists and has clear independent tasks.
It does not provide executable automation or scripts by itself.
It can increase token and subagent usage compared with direct manual execution.
It is less suitable for tightly coupled tasks that require one continuous context.

use_cases.title: Ship a Multi-Step Feature
use_cases.description: Break a prepared implementation plan into reviewed task increments with fresh agent context for each step.

use_cases.title: Maintain Review Discipline
use_cases.description: Add a mandatory review gate after each subagent task so defects are caught before later work depends on them.

use_cases.title: Coordinate AI Coding Workflows
use_cases.description: Use a structured same-session process for implementation, review, fixes, final review, and branch completion.

prompt_templates.title: Start Plan Execution
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin a basic subagent-driven implementation run.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use subagent-driven-development to execute the plan in [plan file]. Work from [repository path] and start with the first independent task.

prompt_templates.title: Run One Task with Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Execute one task and stop after its review result.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this workflow for Task [number] in [plan file]. Dispatch a fresh implementation subagent, request review, and report the review outcome before continuing.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Review Feedback
prompt_templates.scenario: Handle findings from a completed task review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use subagent-driven-development to fix the review findings for Task [number]. Treat critical and important issues as blockers before the next task.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a Full Reviewed Run
prompt_templates.scenario: Execute all tasks, final review, and branch completion.
prompt_templates.prompt: Execute every independent task in [plan file] with fresh subagents, review after each task, run final review, then use the finishing branch workflow.

output_examples.input: Execute a three-task feature plan with review after each task.
output: Task 1 completed with tests passing and no review blockers.
Task 2 required one important fix, which was applied and rechecked.
Task 3 passed review, and final review confirmed the plan requirements.

output_examples.input: Review feedback reports a critical issue after Task 2.
output_examples.output: The workflow stops normal progression, sends the issue to a fix subagent, and resumes only after the critical issue is resolved.
The workflow dispatches a final code review, verifies the whole implementation, and then moves to branch completion steps.

best_practices: Use this skill only after a clear implementation plan is available.
Keep task boundaries independent so each subagent can work with fresh context.
Resolve critical and important review issues before starting the next task.
anti_patterns: Do not use this workflow to invent or rewrite the plan during execution.
Do not dispatch multiple implementation subagents when they may edit the same files.
Do not skip intermediate reviews to save time on risky changes.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It defines a same-session workflow for executing planned development tasks with fresh subagents and review gates.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It is a process guide for agent coordination, review, and task sequencing.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when a plan has mostly independent implementation tasks and quality checks are important.

faq.question: When should I avoid it?
faq.answer: Avoid it when tasks are tightly coupled, the plan is not ready, or one continuous context is required.

faq.question: How does review fit into the workflow?
faq.answer: A code-reviewer subagent reviews each task before the next task starts, and a final review checks the complete result.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
